components.name: Desk Task Button (SVG hotspot)
components.description: Interactive task card on the study desk (M3): a real task becomes the room prop. Only runs in /app when the dashboard passes cards/completedCount/onTaskClick; the landing keeps the static demo art. Geometry is slot-fixed (two task slots + one completed sticker / ghost slot). States: due = Blush card + due-glow circle, today = Paper card, empty slot = dashed Acorn/45 outline card; completedCount <= 0 turns the check-sticker slot into a ghost too. Hover -2.5px lift with stroke deepening to full Acorn (a state ramp, not an authored motion). Keyboard: Enter/Space opens the task, focus shows the world's dashed Acorn outline.

narrative.overview: MN-Qronx's landing world refuses the default SaaS page — no gradient hero, no three equal feature cards, no cascading color words. Instead the homepage is your own room: a Porcelain-paper ground drawn in warm Acorn strokes, isometric furniture walls (moss, sage, oat) and a checkered floor. Every task is an object you place in the room; a due task is the object that lights up while the desk bell beside it swings and rings. Proof, not paint: the wall clock shows real time, "today" is the real date, and every fabricated number wears a Blush MẪU/DEMO chip. The room is scoped by the .room-world wrapper — walking into it swaps font family, selection color, focus ring, and scrollbar to the warm system; an older navy app shell still exists elsewhere and its tokens and glow/beam effects are forbidden inside room surfaces. Both themes are first-class: light is a sunny paper room, dark is the same room at evening with a warm lamp — never blue-black. Milestone 2 extends the world into the guest auth gate (AuthLayout + the RoomUI form skin — Login, Register, Forgot/Reset Password, the Google callback) and nothing bends: fields are 44px paper tiles with a hairline Acorn ring, the halved screen is still one continuous sheet of Porcelain split only by a dotted cord, and errors stay weather-cool — the world survives forms without growing a new voice.
keyCharacteristics: Porcelain paper ground; every seam, stroke, and action is drawn with a warm Acorn pen.
Blush is a state color, not decoration: it marks only the due moment (lit task, its glow, MẪU chips).
Dark mode is a warm evening room (#2B231E paper) lit by a diegetic lamp glow.
Sections breathe on dotted seams (.dot-divider); cards are flat paper with hairline Acorn rings.
Forms wear the landing's skin (RoomUI): every text-entry hit-area is 44px tall and errors publish as bold Ink text, never a new red.
Faults are neutral weather: invalid fields and error panels are Rain — no rose, no red; the due state keeps its color-alarm monopoly.
Baloo 2 (display) + Nunito (body), self-hosted variable fonts with preloads.
Furnishings are flat sticker-props on an isometric floor; the room scene is the world's one authored illustration.
One authored motion: the demo bell circuit (task lights → bell swings → "(mẫu)" toast). Everything else is quiet reveals and ≤2px hover lifts.
Product truth is a design rule: real clock, real date, labeled demo numbers, unchanged routes (/ /app /login /register /pricing, anchors #tinh-nang #cach-hoat-dong #gioi-thieu #lien-he).

rules.name: The Acorn-Pen Rule
rules.body: One pen draws the world. Strokes, rings, seams, dividers, focus outlines, and scrollbars are all rgb(var(--room-acorn)) at varying alpha (0.15–0.9); furniture fields (Oat/Moss/Sage/Rain/Sky) are fills only and never draw outlines.

rules.name: The Due-Only Blush Rule
rules.body: Blush earns its space by meaning: on UI surfaces it marks the due state exclusively — the lit task, its breathing glow, and honest-demo MẪU chips. If a Blush element doesn't tell you something is due, it doesn't belong on app chrome.

rules.name: The Warm-Night Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is the same room at night: Porcelain turns to warm #2B231E, and the lamp (#EECB8A radial, .lamp-glow, dark-only) lights the desk. Never regrade this world onto navy, slate, or blue-black grounds.

rules.name: The Round-Heavy Rule
rules.body: Baloo 2 carries identity even resting at 400 — never letter-space-tighten it, never set headings in uppercase, and never substitute a system display face; Nunito alone carries reading copy.

rules.name: The Dotted Seam Rule
rules.body: Page sections part on the dotted seam — dot-divider (3px strip of spaced Acorn dots, 16px rhythm), echoed by peer dotted rules (list leaders, dotted underlines, dashed frames). Solid hairlines stay inside a single footer; they never replace the page's dotted doctrine.

rules.name: The Host Rule
rules.body: Every viewport names its host — the room in the hero, the cabinet in features, the clothesline in how-it-works — and all surrounding copy serves it. No equal-card wall outside the one waived cabinet shell (see Do's and Don'ts).

rules.name: The Paper-Weight Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat paper at rest; soft black diffuse shadows belong only under raised pills and floating taped cards (a touched field may flash the one focus halo — a response, not a resting shadow) — never colored, never drop-shadowed into "3D card" territory, and the only breathing glow is diegetic room light (Blush due-glow, night lamp).

rules.name: The Rain-Is-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Rain handles error, pending and waiting as neutral weather: an invalid field rings Rain (rest, hover and focus alike), a server error sits on Rain/30 with a bold Ink sentence and a WarningCircle — no rose, no red, never a red field. Color alarm stays the exclusive property of the due state (Blush).

rules.name: The Solid-Wordmark Rule
rules.body: In room surfaces the logotype is plain token lettering — WorldLogo: Baloo 2 700, "MN-" Ink / "Q" Acorn / "ronx" Ink, solid color, no gradient and no glow; the gradient logotype stays quarantined in the old shell's Logo.jsx and never enters room surfaces.

rules.name: The Doorway Rule
rules.body: The auth gate is one room, not a second shell: no card-on-canvas, no glass — the split screen is drawn only by the vertical dotted cord (w-[3px], the same 1.6px dots in a 3×16px column at Acorn/50, wrapper at 80% opacity). Below lg there is no door at all: the form sits alone on the paper under a 30px logo.

dos: Do wrap room-world pages in .room-world and theme everything through room.* Tailwind tokens (bg-room-moss/70, ring-room-acorn/25) so light/dark switch from the single --room-* variable block; never hardcode navy/slate inside it.
Do keep text-on-Blush as .on-blush Ink #4A3B2C in both themes — baked by contrast, not by theme.
Do prove product truth: the wall clock ticks real time, "today" is Intl-formatted real date, and every invented figure wears the Blush MẪU/DEMO chip; never ship an unlabeled sample number.
Do draw all seams as dotted (dot-divider, dotted underlines, dashed frames) and all strokes/rings as Acorn at alpha; hairline solids only inside a footer.

Do stay flat: sticker props stand upright on the floor, motion stays at ≤2px hover lifts and once-only reveals (threshold 0.15, house easing cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), with prefers-reduced-motion honored.

Do carry the two registered exceptions as scoped, not general: the six-drawer cabinet (one shell, waivered nested-cards → LandingPage.jsx) and the authored room illustration (waivered shape-assembled-illustration → RoomScene.jsx).

Do skin every guest form through RoomUI (RoomField/RoomInput/RoomButton/RoomDots) so the one ramp holds everywhere: Acorn/25 rings at rest, Rain rings on invalid, the 44px entry/toggle floor, size lg (h-12) for main actions.

Do keep wall furniture economical: on the auth wall, one taped card ("Nhật ký đúng hạn" — tape Oat/90 turned −5°, ring Acorn/20, floating-card weight beneath) and three Moss blips; the landing rail's three taped cards are that page's furniture, not a wall pattern to replicate.
donts: Don't blue-black the dark theme — Porcelain goes warm #2B231E and the lamp does the lighting; no slate/navy grounds inside the room world.

Don't color-glow, gradient-border, or beam anything (no glow-ring, gradient-border, route-beam, hero-glow, brand gradients) — the world's only breathing light is the Blush due-glow and the night lamp.
Don't pink anything other than the due state on app chrome; Bell gold stays on sounding/burning props, never as a field.
Don't uppercase or letter-space-tighten headings, and don't substitute system display faces — Baloo 2 rest, Nunito reads.
Don't invent hard offset shadows or 3D card tilts; depth is drawn, and shadow vocabulary stays the four paper weights listed above.
Don't paint errors rose or red — Rain/30 panels, Rain rings and bold Ink copy are the whole error kit; only the due state owns an alarm color.
Don't gradient or glow the room wordmark — WorldLogo is solid Baloo 2 token lettering (Ink / Acorn Q / Ink); the gradient logotype stays in the old shell's Logo.jsx.
Don't light the lamp in daylight — .lamp-glow holds opacity 0 until .dark (then 0.55); in light mode the only breathing light is the Blush due-glow.

Don't break the route/label truth: routes / /app /login /register /pricing, anchors #tinh-nang #cach-hoat-dong #gioi-thieu #lien-he, EXTENSION_STORE_URL, DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL stay exactly as shipped; names of unrealized features don't appear as live UI.
